findings.title: Portfolio statement export now exists and carries the wash-sale-adjusted basis through
findings.observed: GET /api/portfolio/statement.md renders a full Markdown statement: totals (cost basis, market value, unrealized, cash split settled/unsettled, total equity), a holdings table with per-symbol priced-as-of dates, weights, and a cash-by-account table with its derivation window. XLV's cost basis in the statement reads $1,149.26 -- the same wash-sale-adjusted figure as /portfolio and the tax API, not the raw $1,123.01 repurchase cost.
findings.expected: A single document of positions, basis, cash and valuation as of a date, usable as an end-of-week record -- present, and consistent with the other surfaces that show the same figures.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the artifact I would actually archive at the end of a trading week. It is only useful if the numbers in it agree with everywhere else I have already checked them, and they do here.

findings.title: Portfolio API money fields are clean decimal strings, no binary-float noise
findings.observed: GET /api/portfolio's position rows carry money fields as clean strings, e.g. XLV: cost_basis '1149.26', basis_per_share '164.18', market_value '1171.59', wash_sale_adjustment '26.25'. No trailing binary-float digits (e.g. no '...097656250'-style artifacts) on any figure checked across all three positions this week.
findings.expected: Money fields precise to the cent as strings, not floats leaking their binary representation.
findings.why_it_matters: A figure I cannot trust past the second decimal is a figure I cannot reconcile against my own fill records; this week every number checked matched to the cent.
